findings.title: creation statement becomes interrogated self-estimate
findings.claim: The opening question converts the human's inherited situation into a questioned self-estimate.
findings.mechanism: The interrogative hamza attached to yaḥsabu retrieves the prior singular human as its hidden subject and turns the next proposition into an answerable thought.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah move from a stated human condition to scrutiny of the human's response.
findings.containment: The ordinary question about power over him remains intact; this finding describes the rhetorical turn into scrutiny.

findings.mechanism: The content complement introduced by an is syntactically governed by the cognition verb, so the denial is presented as a proposition under examination.
findings.reader_payoff: Arrogance appears as a testable claim rather than an isolated feeling.
